verdict.rationale: Vast.ai documents key-only SSH access to instances. Its tooling can manage SSH keys, and you can run your own Docker image with a custom entrypoint, which implies broad control of the environment. A community report confirms renters get a full Linux shell. However, the evidence never explicitly states that users get root privileges, so the root-level half of the story is only implied. missing for 10: explicit documentation of root/sudo access inside instances, a first-party walkthrough of uploading your own public key to an instance, independent hands-on corroboration of root control

support.subject: As a developer, I can SSH into my GPU instance with my own keys and get root-level control of the environment

citations.quote: Vast.ai instances are configured to accept keys only - Password authentication is disabled for improved security.
It encrypts your connection so you can: Log in securely, Run commands remotely, Transfer files without exposing your data
create instances, deploy endpoints, manage SSH keys, check balances, and more
Terminal access with port forwarding and VS Code support
The docker image entrypoint is the main run process, which you can override in the GUI or CLI (--entrypoint).
Renters get a full Linux shell and can deploy images
